See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

New course grade = Current grade + (Replacement score − Existing score) × Weight / 100

A worked example

A course grade of 75% includes an assessment worth 20%, originally scored at 60%. Replacing that mark with 90% adds (90 − 60) × 0.20 = 6 points, giving 81%.

Before you use the result

Your current course grade must already include the old assessment at the stated full-course weight. The tool replaces that mark; it does not add another assessment. It rejects combinations where the implied contribution from other work is outside 0–100%. Permission to replace a mark depends on your instructor.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Will a 10-point assessment improvement raise my course grade by 10?

Only if the assessment is the whole course. At 20% weight, a 10-point improvement raises the course grade by 2 percentage points.

Does this apply an actual regrade?

No. It models a possible replacement. Your instructor decides whether a revised mark is awarded.
